record.paper_title: Twenty Open Problems in Enumeration of Matchings: Progress Report
record.original_question: Determine the number of rhombus tilings of a hexagon with side lengths (a, b+1, c, a+1, b, c+1) after the central triangle has been removed.

evidence.quote: Problem 2: Christian Krattenthaler and Soichi Okada have evaluated the number of rhombus tilings of an (a, b + 1, c, a + 1, b, c + 1)-hexagon with the central triangle removed

artifact.self_contained_problem: Consider a hexagon in the triangular lattice with side lengths (a, b+1, c, a+1, b, c+1) (going around in order), where a, b, c are nonnegative integers. Such a hexagon can be subdivided into unit equilateral triangles, and the unit triangle in the very centre of the hexagon is removed. A rhombus tiling is a tiling of the remaining region by unit rhombi, each consisting of two unit triangles sharing an edge. Determine, in closed form, the number of rhombus tilings of this punctured hexagon.
artifact.status_search_result: Krattenthaler and Okada evaluated the number of rhombus tilings of a hexagon with side lengths (a, b+1, c, a+1, b, c+1) with the central unit triangle removed, obtaining a product formula B(⌈a/2⌉,⌈b/2⌉,⌈c/2⌉)·B(⌈(a+1)/2⌉,⌊b/2⌋,⌈c/2⌉)·B(⌈a/2⌉,⌈(b+1)/2⌉,⌊c/2⌋)·B(⌊a/2⌋,⌈b/2⌉,⌈(c+1)/2⌉), where B(α,β,γ) counts plane partitions in an α×β×γ box. The proof uses nonintersecting lattice paths and a Schur-function identity proved via the Ishikawa–Wakayama minor summation formula. The problem is therefore solved.

status_evidence.title: Enumeration of Tilings of Diamonds and Hexagons with Defects
status_evidence.snippet: Krattenthaler and Okada computed the number of all rhombus tilings of a hexagon with sides a, b+1, c, a+1, b, c+1 with the central triangle removed.
status_evidence.claim: The enumeration was carried out by Krattenthaler and Okada with an explicit product formula.

status_evidence.title: Descending plane partitions and rhombus tilings of a hexagon with triangular hole
status_evidence.snippet: Related work realizing descending plane partitions as cyclically symmetric rhombus tilings of a hexagon with central triangle removed.
status_evidence.claim: Related enumeration results confirm a closed-form solution for the punctured hexagon.
